newsitem.title: UK: Commercial Union single premiums up 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Union single premiums up 20 pct.

text.p: Insurer Commercial Union Plc said on Wednesday single premium sales rose 20 percent in 1996 to 2.36 billion stg. New annual premiums were 22 percent higher at 253 million stg and sales of investment products increased to 276 million from 137 million.
The company said worldwide new business rose by 25 percent to 2.89 billion stg.

Chief executive John Carter said there were strong performances from the group's operations in Britain, France and the Netherlands, plus substantial growth from newer businesses, particularly in Poland and Italy.

In Europe as a whole, new annual premiums were up 23 percent to 49 million stg and new single premiums were 26 percent higher at 434 million stg. There was also substantial growth in individual single premium pensions which increased by 38 percent.

In the United States annual premium sales increased due to growth in individual savings plans and the inclusion of group health insurance. Single premium sales were affected by a fall in sales of annuities due to the relatively low interest rate environment.

The worldwide figures included a contribution of three million stg from Protea Life, which the group bought in South Africa at in November 1996. The firm is also developing a life business in Turkey and in Pakistan, which commenced in July 1996. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
